samples.evidence: Fresh extraction reproduces the sole embedded Sleipnir.ps1 resource. The PE entry method reads that named resource and feeds it into a PowerShell runspace; the 120-method wrapper is consistent with PS2EXE hosting and console/UI plumbing. Inspected the 5710-line script. Gaming/maximum profile UI actions call Add-DefenderExclusions for game paths and processes. Other changes have explicit tweak/profile handlers and local backup/restore functionality. Driver installation downloads through an explicit UI action, requires HTTPS, a valid Authenticode signature with expected vendor naming and a successful restore point before starting the installer. samples.limitations: VT reports 26 malicious detections; these have not been cleared by vendors. The executable signer is a self-issued Sleipnir Local Publisher certificate with an untrusted root, not a verified publisher identity. The script can weaken protection and disrupt host settings. Its comment about preventing cross-host HTTP redirects is stronger than its actual implementation. No blanket safety or security-quality endorsement is made.

samples.evidence: Fresh managed-resource extraction matches the prior extraction. Recomputed the payload archive SHA256 and all 226 manifest member hashes; no extra archive members exist. Manifest consistency proves packaging integrity, not publisher trust. No trusted publisher signature was established. The reader and bundled third-party JavaScript were not exhaustively audited for vulnerabilities or every feature.

samples.evidence: Fresh extraction verifies the embedded app.pak SHA256, then decodes its gzip/custom asset container into index.html, player.html and PeerJS. All 17 managed methods were inspected. Decoded 10979 JavaScript string-wrapper calls using only the isolated string decoder and rotation logic. Inspected file-save, device-key, media, plugin and network paths; application code was not run. Native loopback handlers validate Host and Sec-Fetch-Site; sensitive POST handlers require X-Atoms: 1. Save targets are restricted to configured roots with filename/path checks. The DPAPI-protected value is the application device key. Prior-instance termination targets the same executable identity. Decoded application functionality is encrypted peer-to-peer social/chat/calling. Network paths include the local helper, PeerJS broker and atomsconnections.com version/plugin catalog. Plugin downloads have catalog hash checks and iframe execution uses allow-scripts without allow-same-origin. Media capture is associated with calling/test controls. VT sandbox behavior showing a loopback browser launch, WMI and DPAPI is accounted for by the inspected native methods. No independent hidden credential collector or unrelated payload was found.
samples.limitations: VT reports 31 malicious detections, including Qwexlafiba and GenericKD; the disagreement is unresolved with vendors. X-Atoms: 1 is a fixed header, not a secret authentication token. This corrects the previous review wording. No trusted publisher signature or exact official-release binary comparison was established. Plugins, external services and the entire cryptographic/security design are not certified by this review.
